paragraphs: South Africa’s state-owned logistics company, Transnet, has successfully tested a 7.6-kilometre freight train and claimed to set a new world record.

In a test journey, the colossal train, powered by a combination of electric and diesel locomotives, consisted of 696 empty wagons and covered 860 kilometers between a western coastal port and an inland iron ore mine. According to company officials, the test run surpassed the previous record established in 2001 by a 7.2-kilometre freight train operating in Western Australia.

Transnet presented the successful trial as a significant breakthrough for the nation’s freight transport network, which relies heavily on efficient rail systems to export raw minerals. However, industry observers note that the record claim currently originates directly from Transnet itself, and they await external verification.

paragraphs: A state-owned logistics company in South Africa successfully tested a freight train which is 7.6 kilometres long.

The train consists of 696 empty wagons and recently travelled 860 kilometres from a port on the west coast to a mine. Electric and diesel engines placed along the train provided all the power needed to move it. The company says this train is officially longer than the previous record-holder, an Australian train tested back in 2001.

The company called the successful test a milestone for the country’s train network, which helps move materials across long distances. Although only the company announced the new world record, many people are excited about this big step forward for African railway transportation.
